key_insight: AI systems excelled when comparing contrastive evidence versions, but verifying a scientific claim against a single table or figure remained challenging.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark may inform tools for checking claims in medical literature, but it does not establish clinical reliability or patient-care benefit.
method: Paired authentic claims with supporting and minimally modified, non-supporting tables or figures.
Evaluated support classification and selection between two evidence versions.
Most systems used multimodal large language models with prompting and multi-stage inference.
evidence_signal: Across 180 papers in machine learning, NLP, and medicine, 14 teams submitted 177 runs; the best support-classification system reached 98.1% pair accuracy, while the best standalone evaluator scored 24.3 percentage points lower.
watch_item: All six top-ranked systems relied on contrastive pairs, limiting how well their results represent real-world verification of a single claim and its evidence.
paper_title: Overview of the NTCIR-19 SciClaimEval Task: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers
